source_snapshot.procedure: From BMC run `i2cdetect -y -q 14` and `i2ctransfer -y 14 w3@0x44 0xc0 0x0 0x0 r4`; consult PID1114953.

test_case.test_name: Test connections between BMC I2C-15 and UPHY3 from first PG548 — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify BMC I2C-15 reaches UPHY3 on the first PG548 by reading a defined UPHY register and validating an instance-specific four-byte response without conflating the second PG548.
required_package: PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-15 to Linux bus14 and first-PG548 UPHY3 address0x44
First-PG548 and UPHY3 hardware/firmware/revision identity distinct from second PG548
UPHY vendor definition for three-byte pointer0xc00000 and four returned bytes
Confirmation pointer write is non-mutating, including endian/alignment
Bus14 driver/daemon ownership and approved raw-access window
Timeout/NACK/error criteria, UPHY/bus telemetry and BMC recovery
test_case.test_command: Map logical BMC I2C-15 to Linux bus14 and identify0x44 as first-PG548 UPHY3; confirm pointer0xc00000 is a safe readable register; capture bus owner and first-PG548/UPHY error baseline; avoid broad scan; issue one bounded combined read; decode four bytes against the installed UPHY revision; correlate bus/UPHY telemetry and confirm second-PG548 evidence was not substituted.

safety_gate: Do not use broad `i2cdetect -q` without per-address safety approval

Abort on instance mismatch, invalid response, NACK, timeout, arbitration loss, stuck bus or BMC/UPHY health regression
expected_evidence: PID topology for BMC I2C-15/bus14/first-PG548 UPHY3 at0x44
BMC, first-PG548 and UPHY3 identities/revisions plus bus owner
Vendor pointer0xc00000 definition and expected four-byte field matrix
